title: Past Simple Practice and Writing Questions About a Business Trip
summary: An email completion task, a past simple fill-in exercise based on Rana's clothes company story, and a pair activity where students write questions about Rana's trip to Lebanon and Morocco, covering preferences, food, hotels, and business language.

title: Past Continuous vs Past Simple and Email Writing About a New Company
summary: Students choose between past continuous and past simple in five sentences describing interrupted actions, then write a 100–120 word email to a friend about a recently set-up company, modelling it on Rana's email paragraphs.

title: Reading Comprehension on Technology and Home Fitness Trends
summary: Students read an article about how technology has changed fitness and working out at home, then answer open questions, choose correct options, and complete sentences with vocabulary from the text.
section: Lesson 2: People didn't use to work out at home

title: Comparing Gym Changes with Used to and Writing Interview Questions
summary: Students compare pictures of a gym before and now, describe differences using 'used to' and 'didn't use to', then write five interview questions with 'did … use to' for a businessman who converted his gym into a smart gym.
section: Lesson 2: People didn't use to work out at home

title: Talking About Household Duties and Upcoming Obligations with Have to
summary: Students match sentence halves and pictures, discuss household jobs they must do with a partner, and list six tasks they have to complete in the next week or two, practising 'have to' structures.
section: Lesson 3: How to be the best!

title: Had to Chain Game and Completing Rules for Birchwood International College
summary: In a team game students recall and extend sentences about job obligations using 'had to', then complete sentences about accommodation and course rules at Birchwood International College using have to, don't have to, mustn't, should, or shouldn't.
section: Lesson 3: How to be the best!

title: Expressing Past Regrets with If Only, I Wish, and the Third Conditional
summary: Students match regret stories to three people, then practise forming sentences with 'I wish', 'If only', and the third conditional through dialogue-based fill-in and open-ended completion tasks.

title: Writing Counterfactual Responses with Would Have and Third Conditional
summary: Students complete sentences expressing regret, discuss four situations in pairs about what they would have done, and write their own counterfactual responses using 'would have' and the third conditional.
